newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African new mine safety laws to be launched Wed.
newsitem.headline: S.African new mine safety laws to be launched Wed.

text.p: New legislation to improve safety and training standards on South Africa's mines will come into effect on Wednesday, the National Union of Mineworkers (NUM) said on Tuesday.

The NUM said in a statement the Mine Health and Safety Act together with a new national mine health and safety inspectorate would be launched by Minister of Mineral and Energy Affairs, Penuell Maduna.

The legislation comes in the wake of an accident at the Vaal Reefs Exploration and Mining Co Ltd in 1995 which killed 104 miners when an underground locomotive plummeted down a mine shaft crushing a lift-cage full of workers.
Following a commission of inquiry and inquest into the accident, the country's inspector of mines Derek Baker said new laws would be drawn up to prevent a repeat of the disaster.

The NUM on Tuesday welcomed the new law, under which mines will be required to set up systems to identify, assess and remove all health and safety hazards, but said it had since its inception in 1982 been fighting a losing battle against poor mining standards.
The NUM said the new Act stressed training as a means to improve safety and insisted on consultation between mine management and worker representatives.

"This law lays a base for participatory decision-making process on health and safety issues to take place...The challenge which now lies ahead is to implement the new Act," said Sazi Jonas, the NUM's health and safety education co-ordinator.
